name: Cancel after change rejection (awaiting_approval → cancelled)
description:
The reject side of the first human gate (nl-conversation-intent design D7). A run parked at awaiting_approval carrying run.change.decision == "reject" transitions to cancelled: the authored change is abandoned and a re-triggered issue starts a fresh run (a rework loop that KEEPS the change is a Phase 3 concern, OQ2). Rule-owned transition (G2) — no Go fires it. The decision is stamped by the ONE sanctioned gate writer (approval-adapter) from either the exact `/semdev reject` fast-path or the deterministic apply consumer; this rule never inspects who decided, only that the decision landed.

PHASE GUARD — LOAD-BEARING (architect H1): the agent-run state machine (agentrun.go:46-48) permits a LEGAL executing → cancelled edge. An unguarded reject rule would therefore fire on an ALREADY-APPROVED, ALREADY-EXECUTING run and destroy work the human explicitly approved — the irreversibility asymmetry the design settles: an approval is final once landed (transparency is VISIBILITY, not undo; the downstream PR merge is the real human stop). Gating on agent.run.phase == awaiting_approval confines the cancel to a run still AT the gate, mirroring the resume rule. The guard is ALSO what makes the D13 residual benign: if a decision flips after the run has already left the gate, this rule cannot act on it.

SINGLE-VALUED DECISION (D13, group 8): this rule and run-lifecycle/02 are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION. They previously read two independent booleans and each carried a guard requiring the OTHER absent, because a run could hold BOTH and then fire NEITHER — an unsurfaced permanent wedge that was documented rather than removed. One single-valued fact under replace-by-predicate makes that state unrepresentable; the cross-guards are retired. Pinned by TestOppositeCommandsCannotWedgeTheGate (offline) and the reworked 6.4 conflict journey (end-to-end).

PARK EXCLUSION (repo-wide invariant): like every active lifecycle_transition rule, this one carries `run.awaiting.human length_eq 0` so a run parked toward the human is never swept through a gate before the park is cleared. The guard is inert on the normal path — the change-approval gate is PHASE-based and stamps no run.awaiting.human — and bites only when an ask_human park and a rejection coincide, where holding still is the correct conservative outcome.

FIRING CAP: the transition is terminal for this run (cancelled leaves awaiting_approval, so the conditions can never re-satisfy), hence a single fire per run — the engine's default per-action cap of 3 is never approached and no explicit max_iterations is needed (contrast the conversation routes, which re-fire across the gate's lifetime and must opt out explicitly).

on_enter.reason: human rejected the authored change; abandoning this run

metadata.phase_guard: awaiting_approval only (H1): the legal executing→cancelled edge means an unguarded rule would kill an approved, executing run.
metadata.mutual_exclusion: structural since D13 (group 8): the gate is ONE single-valued fact (run.change.decision), so a run cannot hold both an approve and a reject and the former cross-guards are retired. The old two-boolean design could wedge a run permanently; see the description.
